Model A provides foundational structure via milestone-based escalation, while B extends this into a more accessible four-tier system. Model C introduces temporal variation through weekly billing and VIP inclusion. The owner must select a canonical model to wire the live page; currently, B is recommended as it inherits A’s pricing logic. This selection impacts GSI’s Bayesian inference over customer lifetime value and GSE’s state transitions between preview/demo/live modes. Failure to decide leaves the config inert. The interplay between these models reflects a dualism of accessibility (B) versus rigor (A) and flexibility (C) versus stability. Each model has distinct failure modes: misalignment of tiers leads to conversion loss, unapproved promos cause revenue leakage, and premature operator launch risks feature instability.
